text: The trailer (the deliverable's best moment) is mostly empty night sky. In shots A, D and E the town is a 5-10% strip on the bottom edge or cut off entirely, and the intercepts sit on the top or left frame edge or out of frame (t 231.5 flashes at the very top, t 242-248 the only flash is clipped at the left edge, t 256-258 trails enter from the top-left corner with no town under them). Next to a WARNO/Broken Arrow air-defence trailer shot or a CoH3 store screenshot, these frames read as a black screen with lines.

Shots B1 (impacts south, t 233.6-236) and B2 (Nevatim plain, t 236-241) frame empty desert: a road stub in the foreground, a flat plain, a dark smoke blob and a row of tiny dots for the base. No impact flash, fireball or dust is visible in either at 2 fps, so 7.5 s of the 30 s carry no action.

Every trailer shot is a 2-4 key Hermite segment whose end tangents are zero (paths.js tangent(): ends ease to rest), so each shot accelerates, decelerates to a full stop, then hard-cuts. That reads as 'move, stop, cut' rather than the continuous push/drift of an Iron Harvest or CoH3 cinematic. And no slow motion or hit-stop fired during the trailer: feelLog in trailer/capture.json is empty, so the designed Sling slow-mo beat never landed.

The crest reveal is underpowered. At t=9.5-14.5 Arad is a thin band of lights about 3-4 km away occupying ~25% of the width, on a featureless plain. The 'wadi climb' (t=2.5-8) is smooth rolling dunes with no canyon walls or rim to crest, so there is no moment where the land drops away and the town appears. The IRON WALL title sits directly under the town and competes with it. AoE IV and Iron Harvest intros land the reveal with foreground framing and a much closer, larger subject.

From t=17 to t=24 the intro is a high, slow drone shot over the town as a flat lit grid; the uniform street grid dominates and the shot has no subject or motion accent. It is a long stretch at a fixed tactical-like height before the hand-off.

The siren push toward town is barely readable: frames t=160.25 vs 161.33 differ by a small reframe, while the HUD red wash does all the work. CoH3 and AoE IV beats use a short, clear camera nudge or a shake punch so the moment registers in the body.
applyShake allocates a new THREE.Quaternion every frame while trauma > 0; during the barrage that is a steady GC source.
